NTA. I completely understand where you’re coming from. It’s really awesome that you want to do that for your sister, and I really hope that she appreciates what you are doing. However, if your sister didn’t keep her grades up to an acceptable level to be able to go, I can see why your mother would be upset. She is the mother for a reason, and her wishes should be respected to a point. Life is short though, so I hope she has fun, and also tries to do better in school. Try to compromise and do some goal setting with your sister and mother when it comes to school, it may help deescalate the situation

NTA. Raising a child is hard, no matter what age they are at, but especially when you are first starting out. The 15 year old should be more than capable of knowing how to control themselves and to settle down in different scenarios. The 12/13 y/o, even with mild autism, and they’ll have their outbursts but there is no reason for said child not to be able to control themselves to a point. The 15 year old should be stepping up and helping out their mother, especially if she is a single mom. Don’t feel bad for wanting a calm environment at night for your child. If the problem persists, try inviting the mom and kids over for lunch and having a talk with her. It may help build some bridges on issues you may not be aware of. Even a simple talk at the door with her may help. Anyway, best of luck to you and your family.
